To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the exit place of Brownian motion in domains with horns is a random variable that is not self-similar, (2) for some horns the distribution of the exit place is not a function of the dimension of the domain, (3) the exit place has a power law distribution, and (4) the power law is determined by the geometry of the horn.
for certain horns the asymptotics of the exit probability of a Brownian motion in a domain lying outside the horn is given by a power law, with an exponent that depends on the geometry of the horn.
the logarithm of harmonic measure of the complement of a horn is asymptotically equivalent to a certain integral of a certain function.
